name: SPX, the opening lane's questions: the first hour, read every 5 minutes, measured in tape units
status: read by the tape lane (spx_jev/lane.py, `--lane tape`): asked afresh on every read, 09:35 to 10:30 ET; the answers are summed by questions/spx_lane_hour.json. A placeholder until the research round.
how_to_use: Each group is one JEV request. Every option quotes the label's own words; exactly one escape option, unsure, last. Nothing here is held between reads: the lane has no cadence, so every question is asked on every read.

The net move keeps the sum's own bands in tape units, filled from spx_jev/cuts.py; its options are rose and fell, not the sum's up and down, so the sum never sees its own option words in the state it reads. The range is placed against the same minutes of the day on the prior sessions, in thirds.
The strikes group is a copy of the live doc's weight_side question, word for word; a test keeps it equal to its original.

move_since_read.ask: Since the last read, did price rise, fall or hold, and how far?
move_since_read.why: How far the tape just moved in its own units, in words the sum's options never use.
move_since_read.instructions: Read `tape.move_since_read`. It says how far price ended from the last read in tape units and names the cut it passed, ending 'so it rose big', 'so it rose small', 'so it held', 'so it fell small' or 'so it fell big'. Which is it?

criteria.rose_big: the label ends 'so it rose big': price ended more than the {tape_big_units} cut above the last read
criteria.rose_small: the label ends 'so it rose small': price ended more than the {tape_flat_units} cut and no more than {tape_big_units} of a tape unit above the last read
criteria.held: the label ends 'so it held': price ended within the {tape_flat_units} cut of the last read, either way
criteria.fell_small: the label ends 'so it fell small': price ended more than the {tape_flat_units} cut and no more than {tape_big_units} of a tape unit below the last read
criteria.fell_big: the label ends 'so it fell big': price ended more than the {tape_big_units} cut below the last read
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

range_since_read.ask: Was the range since the last read wide, usual or narrow for this minute?
range_since_read.why: A wide stretch against the same minutes on past sessions is a tape that is moving.
range_since_read.instructions: Read `tape.range_since_read`. Which third for this minute does the label put the range in?

criteria.wide: the range is in the top third for this minute
criteria.usual: the range is in the middle third for this minute
criteria.narrow: the range is in the bottom third for this minute
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

weight_side.ask: Which side of price holds most of the options weight?
weight_side.why: Dealers' hedging leans price toward where the weight sits.
weight_side.instructions: Read `gex.weight_side`. Where does the options weight sit?

criteria.above: more than {even_split_high:.0%} of the options weight sits above price
criteria.below: more than {even_split_high:.0%} of the options weight sits below price
criteria.even: between {even_split_low:.0%} and {even_split_high:.0%} of it sits above price
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call
